subject: ACME - RAG eval follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Robert Chen <robert.chen@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary goal: reduce time-to-answer in customer support KB search and improve grounding (reduce hallucinations) for policy/legal queries.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + custom heuristics; typical query volume ~3k q/day, 99th pct latency target for product is <800ms.
- Success metrics discussed: grounding precision, hallucination rate on high-risk categories, MRR@5 and Recall@10 for retrieval.

Initial recommendations (model & infra fit):
1) Model choices for ACME use-case:
   - Llama2-13B (8-bit quant) for fast, cheap generation with good instruction-following.
   - Mistral-Instruct (7B) for tight latency and lower cost if you prefer smaller footprints.
   - Falcon-40B (quantized) if you want stronger reasoning/longer-context answers for policy docs — useful for high-risk legal queries.

2) Retrieval + reranker approach (RAG):
   - Dense retriever with 1536-d embeddings (high-dim to help recall across short KB snippets).
   - Retriever: Faiss-based ANN or OpenSearch vector with HNSW; chunk size ~500 tokens; overlap 50 tokens.
   - Reranker: cross-encoder on top-k (k=50 recommended) for precision on high-risk categories; bi-encoder only for lower-cost fallbacks.
   - Grounding metrics: we recommend tracking grounding precision (fraction of model answers citing a correct doc), hallucination rate (manual eval on flagged queries), and MRR@5/Recall@10.

3) Evaluation plan (proposed):
   - Run a 1-week offline eval on ~1k realistic queries (we'll provide a seed prompt set).
   - Baseline: your current ES+heuristic approach.
   - Eval variants: Llama2-13B + cross-encoder rerank; Mistral-Instruct + bi-encoder + aggressive caching; Falcon-40B + cross-encoder.
   - Deliverables: benchmark PDF (metrics + sample failure modes), recommended reranker, and a short SOW for a POC.

Attachments: "prompts_and_eval_set.csv" (seed prompts) — see drive link below. I attached a draft SOW for procurement to get you started.

Next steps / asks:
- Robert/Sara: confirm the list of high-risk categories we should prioritize (legal, billing, compliance).
- Legal/procurement: help review the SOW draft (attached).
- Proposal: run the offline eval starting next week; schedule a 30-min sync for initial results (propose Tue 6/29 10am PT).

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_acme_rag_eval

Thanks!

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Attach: SOW_draft.docx

From: Robert Chen <robert.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the eval: 

1) Reranker: can you explain the tradeoffs between a cross-encoder reranker vs a lightweight cross/bi-encoder hybrid? We're sensitive to latency/cost at scale. Would cross-encoder only on top-50 be sufficient?

2) Grounding metrics: you mentioned "grounding precision" and hallucination rate — do you have standard definitions you use (so we can align on labeling)? Also curious if you track grounding coverage (how often any doc is cited) and precision at the answer span vs document level.

3) Benchmarks: can you share a sample of the offline benchmark output (just metrics + a couple of sample Q/A pairs) so our legal folks can scan for risky failure modes?

We can prioritize the legal and billing categories. Also, SOW looks fine at first glance; I'll loop in contracts (contracts@acme.com) for formal review.

— Robert
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Robert Chen <robert.chen@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Great questions — answering inline below and attaching a short benchmark PDF so you have something to show legal: "acme_rag_benchmark_results.pdf" (redacted examples + metrics).

1) Reranker tradeoffs:
   - Cross-encoder: significantly better precision because it jointly encodes query+doc; cost/latency higher. Best used as a second-stage reranker (top-K from a cheap retriever).
   - Bi-encoder: fast and cheap, good for recall and initial filtering. You can run bi-encoder at scale for top-200 then apply cross-encoder on top-50 to balance cost/precision — this is our recommended hybrid.
   - Latency guidance: if you need sub-800ms 99th, run bi-encoder-only for low-risk queries and hybrid (bi-encoder -> cross-encoder top-50) for high-risk categories.

2) Grounding metric defs (proposal):
   - Grounding precision (doc-level): fraction of returned answers where at least one cited doc contains the correct supporting content for the answer (human-labeled).
   - Hallucination rate: fraction of answers containing fabricated facts that contradict the KB (human-labeled; high-risk flag).
   - Grounding coverage: fraction of queries where the system cited at least one doc.
   - Ranking metrics: MRR@5 and Recall@10 on the offline eval set.

3) Benchmarks: attached PDF includes per-variant metrics and 6 redacted Q/A failure cases (we removed PII). Summary: hybrid (bi-encoder -> cross-encoder top-50) reduces hallucination rate by ~30% vs bi-encoder-only at similar recall.

Proposed next steps:
- We'll spin up the offline eval using your seed prompts (attached) and return benchmark PDF by end of week.
- If acceptable, plan a 2-week POC where we run live traffic with canary routing to Redwood Dedicated or your VPC.

I'll also send a short README on labeling instructions for legal to review (how we annotate grounding vs hallucination).

Thanks — looping in Michael and Dylan for technical follow-up.

Best,
Marissa
--
Attach: acme_rag_benchmark_results.pdf, prompts_and_eval_set.csv

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Robert Chen <robert.chen@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Quick technical notes from infra/solutions side: 

- Reranker recommendation: implement a hybrid pipeline: bi-encoder (Faiss HNSW) -> cross-encoder re-rank top-50. For cross-encoder we typically recommend a small/medium cross-encoder (eg. MiniLM-based cross-encoder for cost-sensitive production; Xtreme cross-encoder for stricter precision needs).

- Scoring & grounding heuristics:
  * Use combined score = alpha * retriever_score + beta * reranker_score (we can help tune alpha/beta with a small grid search).
  * For grounding evidence extraction, prefer doc-level citation first, then highlight span passages for legal review. Track both doc-level and span-level grounding precision.

- Performance knobs to meet latency SLOs: prefix caching for common queries, short-circuit bi-encoder answers for low-risk categories, and batching cross-encoder requests with Redwood Optimize settings. We can provide a config template for autoscaling and burst capacity if you go Dedicated.

Next steps (ops):
- I'll produce a short config template (retriever params, chunking, reranker top-K, cache TTLs) and post it to the Drive folder by EOD tomorrow.
- Would like to confirm the eval start date — Marissa proposed next week; Robert, does Tue 6/29 10am PT still work for a short sync to review the PDF and SOW?

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
